goldens.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.
goldens.reasoning: C1 flags the same event-listener guard, which checks ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ while V2 is in use. It names a different consequence (an UnsupportedOperationException crash rather than cleanup being skipped), but it points to the same V1/V2 flag mismatch on the same code.

goldens.comment: In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.
goldens.reasoning: No candidate mentions the owner mismatch in findByName (client.getId() vs the resource server's clientId).

goldens.comment: In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.
goldens.reasoning: No candidate covers getClientsWithPermission returning resource names instead of client IDs.

goldens.comment: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
goldens.reasoning: C2 describes the NPE that happens when getResourceTypeResource returns null and that null is passed to findByResource.

goldens.comment: Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called
goldens.reasoning: No candidate mentions the unused getEvaluationContext method.

candidates: UnsupportedOperationException thrown on client removal when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled - Line 77 guards on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ, but management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled() unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException, crashing the ClientRemovedEvent handler. Same applies to RoleRemovedEvent and GroupRemovedEvent

NullPointerException in hasPermission(ClientModel, String) when getResourceTypeResource returns null - Line 214 finds no resource for the specific client, falls through to line 217 for 'all-clients' resource lookup, and if that also returns null, line 219 passes null resource to findByResource(server, resource) causing NPE

Inconsistent admin-role fallback between canManage(ClientModel) and canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles - canManage checks root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS) before evaluating V2 permissions, but the three map-roles methods skip admin-role checks entirely, breaking the principle that manage is a superset of map-roles
